# M16-S1 (SPEC Sec 14.1): logos build --wasm-features=stack-switching runs
# every goroutine on a WebAssembly continuation instead of resume points.
# The flag is a build flag of logos build and go build and has no help text,
# so go help build stays upstream.
env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local
env GOOS=wasip1
env GOARCH=wasm

# The flag exists on both commands and rejects an unknown feature name.
! logos build -wasm-features=bogus -o $WORK/bogus.wasm .
stderr 'unsupported wasm feature "bogus"'
! go build -wasm-features=bogus -o $WORK/bogus.wasm .
stderr 'unsupported wasm feature "bogus"'
go help build
! stdout 'wasm-features'

# Without the feature the build uses resume points and has no continuation:
# waits keeps its br_table dispatch, pure callees keep none.
logos build -gcflags=-S=2 -o $WORK/plain.wasm .
! stderr 'ContNew'
! stderr '\tResume\t'
stderr 'main\.waits<1> STEXT'
stderr '(?s)main\.waits<1> STEXT[^\n]*\n(\t[^\n]*\n)*\t[^\n]*\tBrTable'
! stderr '(?s)main\.pureLeaf<1> STEXT[^\n]*\n(\t[^\n]*\n)*\t[^\n]*\t(BrTable|ContNew|Resume)\t'
! stderr '(?s)main\.pureSum<1> STEXT[^\n]*\n(\t[^\n]*\n)*\t[^\n]*\t(BrTable|ContNew|Resume)\t'

# With the feature yielding user functions drop dispatch (their calls become
# ACALLCONT): no BrTable remains in waits, pureLeaf, or pureSum. A caller of
# runtime.mcall keeps its resume point even outside the runtime (inlined
# Gosched), because the switch back re-enters that frame, so main keeps its
# BrTable. (cont.new/resume live in runtime wasm_cont_run, which is assembly
# and never appears in compiler -S output; execution below is their proof.)
logos build -wasm-features=stack-switching -gcflags=-S=2 -o $WORK/switch.wasm .
! stderr '(?s)main\.waits<1> STEXT[^\n]*\n(\t[^\n]*\n)*\t[^\n]*\tBrTable'
! stderr '(?s)main\.pureLeaf<1> STEXT[^\n]*\n(\t[^\n]*\n)*\t[^\n]*\t(BrTable|ContNew|Resume)\t'
! stderr '(?s)main\.pureSum<1> STEXT[^\n]*\n(\t[^\n]*\n)*\t[^\n]*\t(BrTable|ContNew|Resume)\t'
stderr '(?s)main\.main<1> STEXT[^\n]*\n(\t[^\n]*\n)*\t[^\n]*\tBrTable'

# The same flag works under go build for a Go main package.
go build -wasm-features=stack-switching -o $WORK/gobuild.wasm .

# Execution under a feature-capable engine proves the mcall switch-back
# resume (no replay of the caller body, switches stays 1), stack growth,
# panic recovery, and goroutine yield end to end with exact output. The
# skips below are environmental and reported as skips, never as proof: set
# LOGOS_REQUIRE_WASMFX=1 to fail instead of skipping when no engine qualifies.
[!exec:node] skip 'node not in PATH'
[!wasmfx] skip 'node lacks --experimental-wasm-wasmfx stack switching'

logos build -wasm-features=stack-switching -o $WORK/exe.wasm .
exec node --experimental-wasm-wasmfx run.mjs $WORK/exe.wasm
stdout '(?m)^12$'
stdout '(?m)^0$'
stdout '(?m)^7$'
stdout '(?m)^recovered: boom$'
stdout '(?m)^1$'
stdout '(?m)^done$'

-- go.mod --
module example.com/switch

go 1.27

-- main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"runtime"
)

//go:noinline
func pureLeaf(a, b int) int { return a*b + 3 }

//go:noinline
func pureSum(x int) int { return pureLeaf(x, 1) + pureLeaf(x, 2) }

//go:noinline
func waits() int {
	c := make(chan int, 1)
	c <- pureSum(2)
	return <-c
}

func grow(n int) int {
	var buf [256]byte
	buf[n%256] = byte(n)
	if n == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	return grow(n-1) + int(buf[n%256]&0)
}

func recovers() (r string) {
	defer func() { r = "recovered: " + fmt.Sprint(recover()) }()
	panic("boom")
}

var switches int

func main() {
	fmt.Println(waits())
	fmt.Println(grow(2000))
	c := make(chan int, 1)
	go func() { c <- 7 }()
	switches++
	runtime.Gosched()
	fmt.Println(<-c)
	fmt.Println(recovers())
	fmt.Println(switches)
	fmt.Println("done")
}

-- run.mjs --
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { WASI } from 'node:wasi';

const wasi = new WASI({ version: 'preview1', args: [], env: {}, returnOnExit: true });
const mod = await WebAssembly.compile(readFileSync(process.argv[2]));
const inst = await WebAssembly.instantiate(mod, wasi.getImportObject());
process.exitCode = wasi.start(inst);
